newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Tunisia eases rules on investment by foreigners.
newsitem.headline: Tunisia eases rules on investment by foreigners.

text.p: Tunisia will allow foreign investors to buy up to 49 percent of the capital of Tunisian firms at the Tunis Stock Exchange without prior authorisation, Tunisian President Zine al-Abidine Ben Ali announced on Saturday.
"We have issued instructions to raise the quota for the purchase of Tunisian shares by foreign investors. This quota will be 49 percent for all purchases," Ben Ali said in a speech at parliament.
Since last year, foreign investors were allowed to buy up to 10 percent of the capital of listed companies on the Tunis Stock Exchange, and up to 30 percent of non-listed companies.
Ben Ali's decision raises the quota to 49 percent for both, Mohamed Ghannouchi, Tunisian Minister of International cooperation and Foreign investment told Reuters.
Under the 1995 law, authorisation from the bourse supervisory body is required for purchases that are above the quota.
